Seglin's classic structure has five parts: first 2–3 paragraphs for hook, set-up and nut graph; the next 4–5 for diagnosis; the next 4–5 for prescription; 1–2 for concession; and one final paragraph for the coda or call to action. — https://www.hks.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/Academic%20Dean's%20Office/communications_program/digital_resources/js_op-ed_classic_structure_11_2_17.pdf 16. That adds up to 12–16 paragraphs. At 750 words, a paragraph averages about 47–63 words. (This is our arithmetic from claim 15, not a figure any source states.) — https://www.hks.harvard.edu/sites/default/

18. On April 27, 2021, *New York Times* Opinion Editor Kathleen Kingsbury retired the label "op-ed" for outside pieces and replaced it with "guest essay". She called "op-ed" "a relic of an older age and an older print newspaper design". https://www.foxnews.com/media/new-york-times-announces-retirement-guest-essays 19. 16. Adults read English non-fiction silently at an average of 238 words per minute, and most read at 175–300 wpm. The source is a meta-analysis of 190 studies with 18,573 participants (Brysbaert 2019, J. Mem. Lang. 109:104047). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jml.2019.104047 17. By that rate, a 750-word op-ed takes about 3.2 minutes to read. The range is about 2.5 to 4.3 minutes. This is derived from claim 16. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jml.2019.104047 18. **In scope:** the convention that caps a guest opinion piece at about 750 words. That covers: - the one-argument discipline the cap forces; - how the word budget is split across the parts of a piece; - where the number came from and how outlet limits changed over time; - edge cases, failure modes, and where sources disagree.

20. **Stripping qualifiers.** Physicist-writer Chad Orzel (2023) says the hard part of writing to length is having to "strip out qualifiers and citations that would seem really important in an academic context". For expert writers the discipline means heavy cutting after drafting, not drafting to length. [S] https://chadorzel.substack.com/p/on-writing-to-length 22. **Permanent oversi

In scope: this report covers the length norm that caps a guest opinion piece at about 750 words. It covers where the norm came from, how the stated limits changed over time, and what the official outlet guidance says.

- **U1 — Why 750 exactly? (gate not met.)** No primary source in this run says who first set 750, or why. There are two competing explanations, and neither is sourced to an originating document: - (a) It inherits the syndicated-column length of about 750 words (claim 17). - (b) It reflects print column-inch economics, meaning the number of words that fit the fixed space opposite the editorials. The column-inch explanation is an inference, not a source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Column_inch - The earliest hard cap found is 700 words, not 750 (claim 6). - **U2 — Is 750 a ceiling or a target?
